style: Vertical 9:16 animated cartoon short. Stylised 3D toon world with 2D 'bean head' cartoon characters: perfectly round white head, thin black stick arms and legs, thick black outline, simple drawn face. The characters are flat 2D cartoon figures, never realistic humans. Warm golden light, rich textured sets (rock layers, gravel, wood, steel). Smooth cinematic camera. Characters keep their mouths closed (silent narrator voice-over plays separately); they show feelings with eyes, brows, sweat drops and body language. No on-screen text except signs and props that belong in the world. No music, no speech.

refs.engineer: Character sheet, full body, front view, plain light background: ENGINEER, young man, perfectly round white bean head with simple dot eyes and small smile, red-and-white striped flat cap, teal vest over white shirt, brown trousers, thin black stick arms and legs. Flat 2D cartoon figure, thick black outline, NOT a realistic human.
refs.boss: Character sheet, full body, front view, plain light background: BOSS, stocky older man, perfectly round white bean head with big brown moustache, brown bowler hat, yellow vest with brown belt, thin black stick arms and legs. Flat 2D cartoon figure, thick black outline, NOT a realistic human.
refs.rival: Character sheet, full body, front view, plain light background: RIVAL engineer, round white bean head with black moustache and a confident grin, black top hat, dark grey coat with red tie, thin black stick arms and legs. Flat 2D cartoon figure, thick black outline, NOT a realistic human.
refs.canyon: Environment reference, vertical, no characters: huge red-orange desert canyon in a stylised 3D toon look, very deep with a dark bottom, two railroad lines on wooden trestle bridges racing toward each other across the gap, two banners (A-LINE blue, B-LINE orange), golden hour sun.
refs.track: Environment reference, vertical, no characters: low close view along a steel railroad track, wooden sleepers, grey gravel ballast, red-orange canyon wall behind, stylised 3D toon look, golden light.

clips.line: He sawed gaps into a railroad every thirty-nine feet.
clips.shot: Low close shot along a railroad track: the ENGINEER sits on one steel rail and saws through it, sawdust flies, a finger-wide cut gap opens in the rail. Camera pulls back along the track and more gaps are visible in the rail ahead, evenly spaced.

clips.line: Two companies are racing to build a railroad across a canyon so deep you can't see the bottom. Whoever finishes first gets the whole country's business.
clips.shot: Wide sweeping shot of a huge red-orange canyon so deep the bottom is black. Two railroad lines on wooden trestles race toward each other from opposite sides, tiny bean-head workers building them, banners A-LINE (blue) and B-LINE (orange). The camera glides forward, tilts down into the bottomless dark, then rises toward the bright sun.

clips.line: He's the youngest engineer on the job. And when his boss sees a finger wide gap between every single rail, his face turns purple.
clips.shot: Medium shot: the young ENGINEER stands proudly on the track with the saw over his shoulder. The BOSS walks into frame, looks down at the finger-wide gap in the rail, and his whole face slowly turns purple with anger, steam puffing from his ears.

clips.line: You're wrecking my railroad. But he won't close a single one. The other one lays rails end to end, perfectly smooth, and finishes first.
clips.shot: On a wooden trestle bridge high in the red canyon at golden hour: the BOSS (yellow vest, brown bowler hat, brown moustache; only his FACE is purple, his body stays yellow-vested) points angrily at the rail, arms flailing; the ENGINEER (red-striped cap, teal vest) calmly crosses his arms and shakes his head, refusing. Then the camera swings to the other bridge where the RIVAL in a black top hat grins as workers lay one perfectly smooth, gap-free rail end to end.

clips.line: Their trains glide across the canyon without a sound, while his go clickety clack over every gap.
clips.shot: Two trains cross the canyon side by side on two bridges: on one a sleek train glides smoothly and silently over seamless rail; on the other a black steam train rattles and shakes over every gap in the rail, bolts jumping, dust puffing. Camera tracks alongside.

clips.line: The newspapers start calling it the Clickety Clack Line, and everyone switches to the quiet trains.
clips.shot: Close-up of a newspaper front page with a giant headline in huge black capital letters reading exactly: CLICKETY CLACK LINE (three words). Then a station platform where a crowd of bean-head townspeople in period clothes turn away from the rattling black train and walk onto the sleek quiet train.

clips.line: Then summer comes, and something weird happens. His gaps start shrinking in May. You can fit a coin in them by July.
clips.shot: Summer: blazing sun, heat haze over the canyon. Close shot of a rail gap: the calendar post beside the track reads MAY and the gap is wide. The calendar flips to JULY and the gap has shrunk to a hairline; the ENGINEER stands a shiny gold coin on edge in the narrow gap and it fits snugly.

clips.line: Barely a sheet of paper, and his boss is thrilled. See, even your gaps know you were wrong.
clips.shot: Close on the rail gap with a sheet of paper wedged snugly in the hairline gap. Exactly two characters appear: the BOSS (yellow vest, brown bowler hat, moustache) leans in, rubs his hands together, thrilled, then points smugly at the ENGINEER (red-striped cap, teal vest), who sighs and looks down.

clips.line: Meanwhile, on the perfect railroad, the rails started groaning in the afternoon sun, pushing against each other like they want out.
clips.shot: The perfect seamless railroad on the other bridge in the afternoon sun: heat shimmer, rails visibly bulging and straining against each other, sweat drops sliding off the steel. Camera low along the track.

clips.line: On the hottest day anyone can remember. His gaps finally close. Rail touching rail.
clips.shot: Blazing hottest day, sun at full strength. Close shot: the two rail ends in the engineer's rail slide together and touch with a small spark, no gap left. The ENGINEER (red-striped cap, teal vest) looks at it and smiles with quiet pride. Wide shot then shows every gap closed and the track straight and fine.

clips.line: Halfway across the canyon, the perfect railroad kicks sideways like a snake, right as a train rolls onto it.
clips.shot: Halfway across the canyon the perfect seamless railroad suddenly buckles and kicks sideways into a clear S-shaped snake curve, rails twisting, just as a plain black steam locomotive (no face) rolls onto it. Camera tracks the train from above.
